# ============================================================
#  TEST DATA. Every name, number and account in this file is
#  invented. Account numbers are zeros and the BIC says TEST,
#  so an invoice made from this file is obvious at a glance.
# ============================================================
#
# Syntax is TOML. The extension is .txt so macOS opens it in TextEdit;
# the script reads the contents, not the extension.

[business]
trading_name = "Example Design Studio"
contact_name = "Alex Example"
email = "alex@studio.example"
phone = "+61 400 000 000"

# Triple quotes let the address span several lines, printed as written.
address = """
1 Example Street
Exampleton VIC 3999
Australia"""


[tax]
# true ONLY once actually registered for GST.
#   false -> no GST line, invoices headed "Invoice"
#   true  -> GST line, invoices headed "Tax Invoice"
# A document headed "tax invoice" while unregistered is a penalty offence.
gst_registered = false
abn = "00 000 000 000"

# The GST rate is fixed at 10% in the script. The ledger stores the GST on
# every line, so past invoices keep their own figures if the rate changes.

# Registration is compulsory at this turnover over any rolling 12 months.
# The run warns once turnover reaches turnover_warn_at of the threshold.
turnover_threshold = 75000
turnover_warn_at = 0.8


[currency]
home = "AUD"

# The one source every foreign exchange rate is taken from. Stay with it: the
# ATO wants rates taken consistently and a record of where they came from.
# The name is written into every ledger row.
source = "TEST DATA — not a real rate source"

# rate is AUD per 1 SEK. as_at MUST equal the invoice date, or the run refuses.
[currency.SEK]
rate = 0.1450
as_at = 2026-12-11


[invoicing]
# The invoice date is the day you run the script. To use a different date —
# say the rate source published nothing today — uncomment this line.
# Remove it again afterwards: a date left over from last month is refused,
# because this month's work is dated after it.
# invoice_date = 2026-11-30

# Invoice numbers are prefix + zero-padded sequence, e.g. INV-0007.
number_prefix = "INV-"
number_padding = 4

# Payment days. Applies to every client; there is no per-client override.
payment_terms_days = 30


# One block per currency received. The invoice shows the block matching the
# client's Currency. A client whose currency has no block stops the run.

[payment]
note = "Please quote the invoice number as the payment reference."

# Domestic AUD transfer.
[payment.AUD]
account_name = "Example Design Studio"
bsb = "000-000"
account_number = "00000000"

# International transfer in Swedish kronor.
[payment.SEK]
account_name = "Example Design Studio"
iban = "SE00 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000"
swift_bic = "TESTSESSXXX"
bank_name = "Example Bank AB"
bank_address = """
1 Example Square
000 00 Exampleville
Sweden"""
